taxa.taxonomy_note: The inventory may use Rosmarinus officinalis. POWO, GBIF and NCBI all treat it as a synonym of Salvia rosmarinus. NCBI has no separate taxid for R. officinalis; it is a name on taxid 39367. NCBI taxid read from the NCBI Taxonomy checklist that GBIF mirrors (dataset fab88965-e69d-4491-a04d-e3198b626e52), because the NCBI pages could not be reached directly (browser rate-limited, E-utilities blocked by robots.txt). WFO id is null because worldfloraonline.org could not be fetched (TLS/robots failure).

pregnancy_lactation.statement: 'The data available are not sufficient to conclude the safety of rosemary preparations used during pregnancy and lactation' (EMA).
pregnancy_lactation.md: 'The data available are not sufficient to conclude the safety of rosemary preparations used during pregnancy and lactation' ([EMA](#term:ema-hmpc)).

allergy.statement: Carnosol is identified as a major allergen in rosemary contact dermatitis.
allergy.md: Carnosol is identified as a major allergen in rosemary [contact dermatitis](#term:contact-allergen).

adverse_event_history.statement: Paediatric camphor seizure reports summarised by EMA.
adverse_event_history.md: Paediatric camphor [seizure](#term:convulsant) reports summarised by EMA.

contraindications.statement: Oral leaf: obstruction of bile duct, cholangitis, liver disease, gallstones [12]
contraindications.md: Oral leaf: obstruction of bile duct, cholangitis, liver disease, gallstones [12](#cite:12)

contraindications.statement: Oil: do not apply to broken or irritated skin [12]
contraindications.md: Oil: do not apply to broken or irritated skin [12](#cite:12)

contraindications.statement: Not recommended: leaf under 12 years, oil under 18 years [12]
contraindications.md: Not recommended: leaf under 12 years, oil under 18 years [12](#cite:12)

constituents_of_concern.threshold_or_limit: EMA toxicity thresholds ~5 mg/kg (insignificant), >30 mg/kg (manifest toxicity)

evidence.claim: Rosemary leaf is traditionally used for dyspepsia and mild gastrointestinal spasm.
evidence.test_article_detail: rosemary leaf (oral); bath additive; cutaneous oil
evidence.outcome_summary: EMA: 'symptomatic relief of dyspepsia and mild spasmodic disorders of the gastrointestinal tract'; bath/oil for 'minor muscular and articular pain'.

md.claim: Rosemary leaf is [traditionally used](#term:traditional-use) for dyspepsia and mild gastrointestinal spasm.
md.outcome_summary: EMA: 'symptomatic relief of dyspepsia and mild spasmodic disorders of the gastrointestinal tract'; bath/oil for 'minor muscular and articular pain'.

gaps: No human efficacy trial found for any indication (EMA: none for approved indications).
